name: session_start
description: [ENTRY — call FIRST, before acting] Use when the user asks to start, load, continue, resume, or open memory for a project. Default mode='cards' loads the owner card, the HARD RULES and the project state card and nothing else; mode='full' adds continuity, insights, rooms, captures and the rest (and is the default when verbose=true, which promises the full JSON context); mode='lite' is a ≤500-token sketch (pull memory on demand via recall()). Read-only: the call leaves the memory store byte-identical (disclosed exceptions: AR_AB_ENABLED=1 writes an A/B arm row, and the hosted server's per-credential activity record). Usage counters and telemetry are queued and recorded before the next write tool (waits at most ~1.5 s), by a 30 s background flush, or when the stdio server's stdin closes or it receives SIGTERM/SIGINT; a crash (kill -9, power loss) before then loses them.

context.description: Optional context for matching cross-project insights

verbose.description: Set true to get full JSON context instead of terse summary

mode.description: Default 'cards' = owner card + HARD RULES (P0s and behaviour policies) + state card + pending-review count, nothing else; 'full' = every section (continuity, insights, rooms, captures, …) and the default when verbose=true; 'lite' = ≤500-token sketch, pull on demand.

name: session_end
description: [ON SAVE/EXIT — YOU must call this; nothing auto-saves] Use when the user asks to save, checkpoint, summarize, end, retain, or persist the current session. Optionally pass close_phase / open_phase to update the project pipeline narrative spine in the same call.

summary.description: What happened this session. Simple session: 2-3 sentences. Multi-phase session: one paragraph per completed phase (e.g. 'Phase 1 — Name: what happened. Phase 2 — Name: what happened. Decisions: X. Blockers: Y.'). Never compress a multi-phase session to 2 sentences — it makes the journal useless.

trajectory.description: Where is the work heading next.

close_phase.description: Close the currently active pipeline phase as part of this save. Provide all three reflection fields explicitly — never auto-generated.

open_phase.description: Open a new pipeline phase as part of this save (e.g. when a watershed session pivots into the next strategic direction).

state.description: Project state card, REWRITTEN every save and loaded by the next session_start. Omitted fields carry forward; [] clears a list. Soft caps (overflow truncated with … and listed in state_card.truncated): goal ≤300 chars, open_decisions ≤5×160, blockers ≤5×160, next ≤300 (defaults to trajectory), pointers ≤8×200 (paths/URLs). Hard limits (beyond these the whole save is rejected): goal and next ≤1200 chars; open_decisions and blockers ≤20 items × 640 chars; pointers ≤20 items × 800 chars.

name: remember
description: [MID-SESSION WRITE — single fact/decision; saying it is not saving it] Use when the user asks to remember, store, note, or save a specific decision, fact, or insight.

context.description: Routing hint. Values: 'architecture' or 'decision' → palace/architecture room. 'blocker' or 'blocked' → palace/blockers room. 'goal' → palace/goals room. 'lesson' or 'insight' → awareness. 'qa' or 'capture' → Q&A log. Omit for auto-classification. Note: bug/fix/error content previously routed to standalone knowledge/ dir now routes to journal (purity-census-2026-07-05: knowledge/ is write-only, not surfaced by recall or session_start).

name: recall
description: [RETRIEVE — use freely, any time] Use when the user asks to recall, search, find, or look up previous memory, context, or decisions. Read-only: the call leaves the memory store byte-identical (disclosed exceptions: the hosted server's per-credential activity record). Usage counters and any feedback ratings are queued and recorded after the call: before the next write tool (waits at most ~1.5 s), by a 30 s background flush, or when the stdio server's stdin closes or it receives SIGTERM/SIGINT. A crash (kill -9, power loss) before then loses them.

feedback.description: Rate previous recall results to improve future ranking. Applied AFTER this call (queued; flushed before the next write tool, by the 30 s background flush, or on stdin close or SIGTERM/SIGINT): it never changes this call's results, and a crash (kill -9, power loss) before the next flush loses it. Pass {id, useful:true} for each result you actually used; {id, useful:false} for noise.

useful.description: Was this result useful? true=boost, false=penalize in future recalls.

since.description: ISO date ("2026-05-01") or relative duration ("7d"). Filters journal results.

name: check
description: [MID-SESSION — safe any time; for alignment, before risky decisions] Use when the user asks to validate understanding, verify alignment, or check if their interpretation matches the human's intent. Also call BEFORE a high-risk action — publish, deploy, delete, credential exposure, external send/message, or any other irreversible write — passing `action_description` (one sentence, what you're about to do). Returns matching corrections/rules/insights plus a `verdict`: `blocked` means an authoritative correction OVERRIDES the plan — read it before proceeding. To RECORD a durable human correction, pass `human_correction` as the STRUCTURED object {rule, why, applies_when} — a plain string is only STAGED for later review, never activated.

goal.description: The goal or decision question you're checking alignment on. Required for alignment checks; optional when recording a pure decision trail (prior/posterior/evidence).

understanding.description: Alias for goal — use when saying 'check my understanding: X'. Provide either goal or understanding.

confidence.description: How confident you are. Defaults to medium.

human_correction.description: After human responds: what they actually wanted. Pass the OBJECT form {rule, why, applies_when} to activate a durable correction; a plain string is only staged for review.

anyOf.description: LEGACY string form — STAGED to the pending-review store, NOT activated. Prefer the object form.
STRUCTURED correction — the ONLY form that reaches the active corrections ledger. Incomplete input is rejected with an agent_instruction explaining the fix.

rule.description: ONE imperative, self-contained sentence stating the durable behavior (e.g. "Never publish without explicit owner approval"). Questions/status statements are rejected.

why.description: Concrete evidence behind the rule — what happened or what the human said. Required for activation.

applies_when.description: 1-5 REAL context keywords (topics/domains, e.g. ["git","deploy"]) — sentence fragments are rejected.

pending_id.description: Id of a staged pending correction (from session_start's pending_corrections or a prior check result) — resolves it: promoted with a valid {rule,why,applies_when}, or discarded with resolution:'reject'.

resolution.description: With pending_id: 'promote' (default; requires valid rule/why/applies_when) or 'reject' (discards the staged item; `why` doubles as the reject reason).

delta.description: The gap between your understanding and reality (or 'none').

prior.description: Initial probability estimate (0-1). Start of Bayesian decision trail.

evidence.description: Evidence collected since prior. Each entry shifts probability.

direction.description: Does this support or weaken the hypothesis?

outcome.description: Final decision result: 'confirmed', 'rejected', 'partial', or free text. Triggers decision trail persistence.

decision_id.description: Link multiple check calls to the same decision. Auto-generated if not provided.

action_description.description: What you're about to DO, one sentence — pass this before publish/deploy/delete/credential/external-send/irreversible-write actions. Returns matching corrections/rules/insights on the result's `action_check` field, with `verdict: "blocked"` when an authoritative correction overrides the plan.
